chunks: One of our companions, his chain having dropped from me, narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not leave out anything that is needed except that He taught it to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So, from His teaching him was that he ascended the pulpit one day, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people! Jibraeel came to me from the Subtle, the All-Knowing, and said: 'The virgins are like fruit on a tree. When the fruit ripens and is not picked, the sun spoils it and the winds scatter it. And so are the virgins when they reach what women reach; there is no cure for them except the husband, otherwise there is no safety for them from corruption, for they are human beings.'

He said: So a man stood up to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, whom should we marry them to?' He said, 'Their matches.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and who are their matches?' He said, 'The believers are matches for one another. The believers are matches for one another.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling regarding the marriage of virgins according to the Prophet's teaching in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic wisdom regarding the natural physiological needs of women, using the metaphor of unharvested fruit to emphasize that marriage is the divinely prescribed remedy to prevent moral corruption. It establishes the principle of 'kafa'ah' (compatibility), defining it broadly as shared faith, which underscores the spiritual equality of believers in marital selection within Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
One of our companions, his chain having dropped from me, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not neglect anything from what is needed to except that He<sup>azwj</sup> Taught it to His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So, from His<sup>azwj</sup> Teaching him<sup>saww</sup> was that he<sup>saww</sup> ascended the Pulpit one day, so he<sup>saww</sup> Praised Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Extolled Him<sup>azwj</sup>, then said: ‘O you people! Jibraeel<sup>saww</sup> came unto me<sup>saww</sup> from the Subtle, the All-Knowing, so he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘The virgins are at the status of the fruit upon the tree. When the fruits ripen and if you do not pick them, they would be spoilt by the sun and scattered by the flowing wind; and similar to that are the virgins, when they become aware what the women are aware of, so there is no cure for them except for the husband, or else there is no safety upon them from the spoiling, for they are human beings’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So a man stood up to him<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! So whom they should marry?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘To their matches (nobles ones)’. So he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! And who are their matches?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Believers are the matches of each other! The Believers are matches of each other!’.
en.sarwar: 2. Certain persons of our people whose chain of narrators I have missed have narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has taught to His Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, everything that is needed. Of such teachings is what he spoke one day from the pulpit. He (the Messenger of Allah) praised Allah and spoke of His glory, then said, ‘O people, Jibril came to me from the most Subtle, most Aware One and said, “The virgins are like ripe fruit on the tree which if not plucked up become spoiled because of the sun, and winds scatter them away. So also are virgins when they experience what women experience; then there is no medicine for them except husbands, otherwise, one is not safe from their getting spoiled because they are human beings.’”

One man then stood up and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, to whom must we give in marriage?’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Give them in marriage to their matches.’ He then asked, ‘Who is a match?’ He (the Messenger of Allah) replied, ‘The believers are each other’s match.’”
